doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Money with Maynard and saving on the road
summary: He did not haggle over pay, following his parents' advice; Maynard paid hotels and he saved money traveling like a tourist.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Gee, timing. In retrospect, like when a gig like that happens and you meet somebody and then you get the call, do you quibble about money?

No. No. My parents had always said to me, because there was a huge recession in New Zealand when gasoline was rationed and all this kind of stuff. And a lot of people were unemployed. And when I was of employable age, my parents said, “if you get a job, be thankful you’ve got the job and work out the money later.” And so Maynard was fine with me. He was picking up the hotels, which was a huge thing. And I was able to save quite a lot of money with Maynard. And I lived pretty thriftily on the road and I approached it as a tourist so I wouldn’t go crazy. So I was taking pictures all over the place and when someone would rent a car for a couple of days we’d go out and see the sights and take the local car, which was nice.
